elements.problem: Two parts, both encoded. rule_level_problems.problem: The rule encodes two of the page's four 'test even without symptoms' triggers (contact, screening CXR) but not the other two (DS-TB in the last 2 years; PLHIV). Both omitted triggers are expressible as patient state (active_condition / history with a 2-year onset window; active_condition HIV infection) even though their timing schedules are not. Asymptomatic PLHIV and recently treated patients therefore never reach the suspected-TB state on this page.

summary: The red box is encoded cleanly: all 13 danger-sign criteria are present in the Urgent rule with existing SNOMED concepts, correct thresholds and directions, the trigger is the possible-TB diagnosis, and every check_for finding is consumed. The most consequential problems are (1) the possible-TB rule omits two of the page's four asymptomatic test triggers (TB in the last 2 years, PLHIV), (2) 'unable to walk unaided' is encoded as the stricter Unable to walk, and (3) the pulse measurement uses 'Pulse, function' rather than 'Heart rate', which may not match the recorded vital. The hemoptysis volume threshold and the lab-result-driven diagnoses (LAM, DST) are not representable or outside the house standard and are noted at low severity.
